satellites.title: The Moon Is the Wanting
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen: 月，闕也。大陰之精 — “月 is 闕, the gap: the essence of great yin.” The moon is named for its waning, against 日，實也, the sun that is always full.
satellites.caveat: A sound gloss (聲訓) is Han hermeneutics, not historical etymology.

satellites.title: The Finger Pointing at the Moon
satellites.evidence: The Śūraṅgama Sūtra: 如人以手指月示人，彼人因指當應看月 — “as when someone points at the moon to show it to another, that person should follow the finger and look at the moon.” To take the finger for the moon is to lose both.

checked.note: 汝等尚以緣心聽法，此法亦緣，非得法性。如人以手指月示人，彼人因指當應看月
